common_name: Phoenix Tears Goji Berry (Compact High-Yield Goji Cultivar)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root stock in spring after frost danger; Phoenix Tears is a named goji selection bred for heavier fruit set and a more manageable habit than seed-grown goji.

directions: Plant in well-drained loam with a pH of 6.5–8.0 in full sun; goji tolerates poor, alkaline soils where other fruiting shrubs struggle. Phoenix Tears is a named goji cultivar selected for heavy, reliable fruit production and elongated, bright red-orange berries with the tart-sweet flavor typical of the species, on arching, slightly thorny canes that can be left as a loose shrub or trained to a central leader with staking. Prune lightly after fruiting to maintain shape and encourage new fruiting laterals for the following season. Harvest ripe berries by gently rolling the stem between your fingers rather than pulling directly on the fruit, since the sap can stain skin and clothing.

common_name: Big Lifeberry Goji (Large-Fruited Compact Patio Goji)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root stock in spring after frost danger; Big Lifeberry is a compact, breeding-program goji cultivar suited to smaller gardens and large containers as well as open ground.

directions: Plant in well-drained loam with a pH of 6.5–8.0 in full sun; goji tolerates poor, alkaline soils where other fruiting shrubs struggle. Big Lifeberry is a modern breeding-program goji selection producing notably larger berries than seed-grown goji, on a more compact, better-branched plant that fruits at a younger age and fits large containers as well as garden beds. Its bushier, less sprawling habit than wild-type goji makes it easier to manage without the loose, arching growth typical of the species. Prune lightly after fruiting to maintain shape and encourage new fruiting laterals; harvest ripe berries by gently rolling the stem between your fingers rather than pulling on the fruit directly, since the sap can stain.

common_name: Purple Heart Pomegranate (Deep Purple-Red Aril Pomegranate)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or grafted trees in spring in full sun in well-drained soil; pomegranates tolerate drought, alkaline soils, and heat, making them well suited to zone 9 Gulf Coast gardens.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; pomegranates tolerate drought, alkaline soils, and heat, harvesting when the skin deepens to full color and the fruit sounds hollow when tapped. Purple Heart bears fruit with a deep purple-red skin blush and arils that run notably darker than the bright ruby-red of most pomegranate cultivars, with rich, sweet-tart flavor and juice that stains a deep, saturated purple-red. Its striking dark coloring makes it a distinctive choice among pomegranate cultivars both for fresh eating and for juice with an unusually deep color. Prune to an open, vase-shaped form in the early years and remove root suckers regularly, since pomegranates sucker readily from the base; established trees are long-lived and require little routine care.
